name: Build the annual capital program and the five-year Distribution System Plan
summary: Each year the asset management and planning engineers turn condition results, capacity studies, connection forecasts and City road works into a ranked list of capital projects and programs, then cut and pace it until it fits the rate plan, the crews and contractors available and the financing. The list goes through engineering managers, the engineering director, the executive team and the board before it is loaded into the ERP and released for delivery. One year in five the program becomes the Distribution System Plan filed with the rate application, which adds months of drafting, regional planning letters and customer engagement. The work is slow because needs exceed the envelope by tens of millions of dollars, prioritization is done in spreadsheets outside the investment planning tool, and each cut sends the portfolio back for another iteration.

baseline.org_archetype: A city-owned Ontario local distribution company serving about 346,000 customers with about 570 staff and an 80-person asset management and engineering division, modelled mainly on Hydro Ottawa.
baseline.notes: Reference period 2019 to 2022. The 2021-2025 DSP was filed in February 2020 and updated in May 2020; ordinary annual cycles ran in 2019 (with the DSP), 2020, 2021 and 2022.

unit_of_work: one annual capital program (and, one year in five, the Distribution System Plan)
trigger: Finance issues the annual budget call and planning calendar in spring, once the year's asset condition results and planning studies are available.
end_state: The board has approved the capital budget, projects and programs are set up in the ERP and released to project delivery and operations; in a filing year the DSP has been handed to regulatory affairs for the rate application.

volume.seasonality: One cycle a year, running from about April to December. In a rate-filing year (2019 for the 2021-2025 plan) DSP drafting and customer engagement start a year or more before filing.

evidence.note: One capital budget a year; a five-year DSP filed with each rebasing application (2021-2025 plan filed in 2020).

Seven asset engineers and analysts; about a tenth of their year goes to building and re-ranking the renewal programs. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Eight planning engineers; capacity project lists, DSP chapters in filing years and estimates. The rest of their time is planning studies, connections and protection. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Forecasts System Access spending (subdivisions, commercial connections, relocations) for the plan. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Four engineering managers sit on the challenge workshops and own the release. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Director rationalizes the portfolio to the envelope and presents to executives. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.
Confirms crew, contractor and outage capacity to deliver the plan. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

Prices the portfolio, overheads, capitalized labour and rate impact, prepares the board package and loads the ERP. Loaded cost = 2019-2022 hourly wage x 1.40 (benefits, OMERS pension, payroll taxes and overhead), as in the organisation file.

systems.name: Copperleaf C55 asset investment planning (AIP) software
Asset condition and health index analytics
ERP: general ledger, work orders, purchasing, inventory, fixed assets
Geographic information system (asset and network model)
Document management and engineering drawing repository

steps.name: Issue planning calendar and envelope guidance
steps.description: The engineering manager responsible for planning takes the budget call from finance and the prior year's plan, sets dates for program submissions, workshops and executive review, and sends each program owner the preliminary capital envelope by investment category. The memo restates the DSP run rate the OEB approved so owners know the target before they build needs.

evidence.note: Capital plan built against the DSP envelope; calendar timing is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Gather condition results, studies and reliability data
steps.description: An asset analyst collects the year's asset condition assessment and renewal candidate lists, the planning studies recommending capacity work, the worst-feeder and reliability report, and the open project carry-over list from the ERP. Late inputs are chased by email; the ACA usually arrives last.

evidence.note: Inputs named in the DSP description; waits estimated.

steps.name: Request City road works and relocation plans
steps.description: A planning engineer asks the City for its multi-year road reconstruction, rapid transit and sewer program and lists which Hydro plant will have to be relocated or can be renewed in the same trench. The City's program and dates often change, so the engineer flags each item as firm or tentative.

evidence.note: Relocations for light rail and downtown arteries were part of the 2016-2020 program; timing estimated.

steps.name: City confirms its road works program
steps.description: The City's infrastructure office returns its draft multi-year program with tentative construction years. Hydro waits for this before fixing relocation and joint-trench renewal projects.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from common Ontario distributor practice.

steps.name: Build renewal needs forecast by program
steps.description: Asset analysts each take a group of programs (poles, cables, underground transformers, switchgear, station transformers and switchgear, protection) and size the engineering need from health index ranks, failure trends and unit costs. Each writes a short program sheet with volumes, cost and risk if deferred. The forecast reflects what engineering judges necessary, before any envelope is applied.

error.defect_description: Unit cost or volume carried from an old program sheet; a program is sized on stale health index results.

evidence.note: Rationalization started from an engineering asset needs forecast that took account of age, safety and reliability; effort estimated.

steps.name: Prepare capacity and system service project list
steps.description: Planning engineers turn the studies' recommendations into projects: new feeders, station transformer upgrades, voltage conversion, load transfers, SCADA and automation. For each they write scope, in-service year, a class 4 or 5 estimate and the consequence of delay, such as stations above planning capacity.

error.defect_description: Estimate left at concept level; in-service date not tied to the regional plan or the transmitter's work.

evidence.note: Capacity constraints are one of the top four 2021-2025 drivers; stations and feeders over planning capacity are scorecard measures.

steps.name: Forecast System Access spending
steps.description: Two connections engineers forecast subdivision, commercial and infill connection spending and capital contributions from the development pipeline, signed offers and City relocations. They net contributions from gross cost because developer payments offset a large part of the category.

evidence.note: System Access averaged $40.7M gross with $24-25M of capital contributions a year in the 2021-2025 plan.

steps.name: Compile general plant requests
steps.description: The budget analyst collects fleet, facilities, tools and IT requests from their owners on a standard template and checks each has a business case and a cash flow by year.

evidence.note: General Plant is a separate investment category ($17.1M a year planned) with fleet, IT and facilities programs.

steps.name: Load candidate investments into the planning tool
steps.description: An asset analyst enters each candidate project and program into the C55 investment planning tool with cost by year, investment category, driver and the risk and value scores from the health index and reliability data. Station risk costs come from a separate spreadsheet and are typed in.

error.defect_description: Duplicate or mis-categorized investment; risk score typed against the wrong asset.

evidence.note: Health index results were loaded into Copperleaf C55 for risk evaluation in 2019; manual transfers noted by METSCO.

steps.name: Prioritize into a draft portfolio
steps.description: The analyst exports the candidates and ranks them in a spreadsheet by risk reduced per dollar, mandatory status (connections, relocations, regulatory) and program pacing, then draws a cut line at the envelope. Items below the line are listed with the risk of deferral.

error.defect_description: Formula or sort error in the ranking workbook moves a project across the cut line.

evidence.note: METSCO found investment prioritization was still done in Excel outside C55 in 2019.

steps.name: Engineering challenge workshop
steps.description: The four engineering managers meet with the analysts and planners, walk through each program and project above and below the line, challenge volumes and estimates, and agree trades between renewal, capacity and access. Items found wrong go back for rework.

control.basis: Asset management policy: engineering review of the capital portfolio before executive submission

evidence.note: Typical cross-department challenge session at Ontario LDCs; share needing rework estimated.

steps.name: Check delivery capacity with operations
steps.description: The engineering director's staff send the draft plan to the operations director, who checks crew hours, contractor capacity, outage windows and material lead times by quarter. Operations marks work that cannot be built in the year, for example where connections and storm work will take the same crews.

evidence.note: Resource capacity is a named constraint in the plan; 2021 work was deferred for labour, material and outage limits.

steps.name: Price the portfolio and its rate impact
steps.description: The budget analyst adds overheads, capitalized labour and contributions, spreads cash flows into in-service additions by year, and runs the revenue requirement and bill impact model against the rate plan. She flags years where additions exceed the approved amounts and would fall into the capital variance account.

error.defect_description: Overhead rate or in-service timing assumption wrong, misstating additions.

evidence.note: Capital additions tracked by category against approved amounts with a variance account for underspending.

steps.name: Director rationalizes to the envelope
steps.description: The engineering director compares priced needs with the envelope, safety and reliability risk, customer preferences and financing, and decides which programs to pace down or defer. When the gap is large she sends the analysts back to re-rank; the 2021-2025 review removed about $50M a year from the engineering need.

evidence.note: Rationalization reduced the forecast by about $50M a year after several iterations; iteration share estimated.

steps.name: Executive team review
steps.description: The vice-presidents and the CEO review the capital envelope with the operating budget and financing plan, question large projects and deferrals, and either accept it or ask for a lower total. In a rebasing year they also decide the DSP run rate to file.

control.basis: Corporate delegation of authority: executive approval of the capital envelope

evidence.note: Plan iterated for rate impacts and financing; one rebasing filing every five years. Shares estimated.

steps.name: Draft the DSP and material investment narratives
steps.description: In a filing year, planning engineers write the Distribution System Plan to the OEB's Chapter 5 format: asset management process, condition and capability assessments, five historical and five forecast years by category, and a justification for every project or program over the materiality threshold. Each engineer writes several chapters and cross-checks every figure against the C55 and ERP extracts.

error.defect_description: Figures in narrative tables disagree with the appendices or with each other.

control.basis: OEB Filing Requirements for Electricity Distribution Rate Applications, Chapter 5 (Distribution System Plan)

evidence.note: Chapter 5 content requirements; effort estimated (Hydro Ottawa's DSP ran to several hundred pages with attachments).

steps.name: Obtain regional planning status from IESO and transmitter
steps.description: The utility asks the IESO and the transmitter for letters or report extracts that confirm the status of the Needs Assessment, IRRP and Regional Infrastructure Plan and the station work they expect, so the DSP can show coordinated planning. Replies come on their schedule.

evidence.note: Section 5.2.2 requires regional planning deliverables or their status; the Ottawa IRRP was in progress in 2019-2020.

steps.name: Customer engagement on plan options
steps.description: A research firm hired by the utility runs workbook surveys and focus groups that show customers the reliability and bill trade-off of different capital levels. Results come back after several weeks of fieldwork; the engagement for Hydro Ottawa's 2021-2025 plan drew nearly 21,000 customer responses.

evidence.note: Nearly 21,000 customers responded; customers preferred maintained reliability at little or no added cost. Durations estimated.

steps.name: Pace the plan to engagement results
steps.description: The director reviews what customers chose, moves programs between years to smooth bill impact, and confirms the five-year run rate with the executive sponsor. The DSP tables are re-cut to match.

evidence.note: Plan paced to minimize rate impacts in response to customer feedback.

steps.name: Regulatory review and integration into the rate application
steps.description: Regulatory analysts check the DSP against the filing requirements and the other exhibits, reconcile capital tables with the revenue requirement model and OEB appendices, and send inconsistencies back to the planners. The cleaned DSP becomes Exhibit 2-4-3 of the application.

control.basis: OEB Filing Requirements, Chapters 2 and 5: consistency of capital appendices and DSP

evidence.note: DSP filed as Exhibit 2-4-3; review effort estimated.

steps.name: Prepare the board capital budget package
steps.description: The budget analyst writes the capital section of the budget book: totals by category and program, major projects, deferrals and their risks, and the financing need, with slides for the director to present.

evidence.note: Standard annual board budget package practice at a municipally owned utility.

steps.name: Board approves the capital budget
steps.description: The CEO presents the capital budget to the board of directors at its scheduled meeting, usually in late fall. The board approves it, or occasionally asks management to bring back a lower figure.

control.basis: Board of directors approval of the annual capital budget under the shareholder declaration

next.condition: board asks for a lower figure

evidence.note: Board approval of the annual budget is standard governance for a municipally owned utility; meeting timing estimated.

steps.name: Load the approved budget into the ERP
steps.description: The budget analyst creates or reopens budget programs and project shells in the ERP with the approved amounts by year, cost centre and investment category, so project managers can raise work orders and requisitions in January.

error.defect_description: Amount keyed to the wrong program or year.

evidence.note: Spending is tracked by about 35 budget programs in the ERP against approved amounts.

steps.name: Release the program to delivery and operations
steps.description: The engineering manager sends the approved project and program list with priorities and target in-service quarters to project delivery, work planning and the field programs, and posts it in the document store. Deferred items are recorded for next year's cycle.

evidence.note: Released plan is then measured as DSP implementation progress.

exceptions.name: Envelope gap needs further ranking iterations
exceptions.description: Priced needs exceed the envelope or the executive team asks for a lower total, so the analysts re-rank and the director cuts again.

exceptions.name: Distribution System Plan filing year
exceptions.description: One year in five the plan is written up as the DSP, regional planning letters are gathered, customers are engaged and regulatory affairs integrates it into the rate application.

exceptions.name: Board sends the budget back
exceptions.description: The board asks for a lower capital figure, usually in a year of rate or financing pressure.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from budget call to release of the approved program
benchmarks.population: Annual capital planning cycles at a large Ontario LDC, 2019-2022, including one DSP filing year in five

evidence.note: Author's estimate: budget call in spring, board approval in November or December, release in December or January; a DSP year adds about four to six months of drafting and engagement.

benchmarks.unit: CAD million per year removed from the engineering asset needs forecast
share of planned System Renewal and System Service spending completed in 2021

pain_points.description: Prioritization runs in spreadsheets exported from the investment planning tool, so every iteration means re-exporting, re-ranking and re-checking formulas by hand.

evidence.note: METSCO 2019: health index results loaded to C55 but prioritization still done in Excel.

pain_points.description: Engineering need exceeds the affordable envelope by a wide margin, so the portfolio cycles between analysts, director and executives several times.

evidence.note: About $50M a year cut from the needs forecast.

pain_points.description: The plan assumes crew, contractor and material capacity that does not always appear, so released work is deferred and DSP implementation falls short.

evidence.note: 92% DSP implementation in 2021, deferrals for labour, material and pandemic outage limits.

pain_points.description: In filing years the same engineers write the DSP while running the annual plan, and figures drift between narrative, appendices and models.

evidence.note: Common experience with large OEB DSP filings.

assumptions: The cycle is started by finance's annual budget call (fin-budget). Planning studies, asset condition results, reliability reports and the City's road program are standing inputs, not triggers; the organisation file lists planning_study and asset_condition as triggers.
The capital plan is sent to fin-rate-application only in DSP filing years (about one in five); the interface is listed under the single 'released' outcome.

Copperleaf C55 is added as a system because the organisation file's asset-analytics entry describes only health index analytics; the model company used C55 for investment planning and Excel for prioritization in 2019 (ho_irr).

Connections engineers and the operations director take part although the organisation file's process map does not list them; regulatory analysts and the CEO take part in DSP years and at board approval.
Touch time on drafting and analysis steps is counted as continuous minutes by the simulator; the long waits before those steps stand for the weeks over which part-time effort is spread.
The simulated median cycle is compared with a tier C benchmark of 230 days; ordinary years run about 7 months and DSP years 11 to 13 months from budget call to release.
FTE figures cover only time spent building the plan; the staffing check uses 130 productive hours a month and the single annual case.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, UPDATED Exhibit 1-1-8 Executive Summary (EB-2019-0261), May 5, 2020
sources.supports: DSP is the culmination of business strategy, customer engagement, capital investment, asset management and regional planning processes; 2021-2025 capital by OEB category averaging $100.8M net a year; forecast went through iterations for priority, customer preference, rate impacts, resource capacity and financing; 19% of assets past expected service life (51% of stations, 23% of overhead assets), 17% in poor or very poor condition; custom scorecard measures for stations and feeders exceeding planning capacity; nearly 21,000 customers took part in rate engagement.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2021-2025 Custom IR Application, UPDATED Exhibit 2 (rate base), including Exhibit 2-4-1 Capital Expenditure Summary (EB-2019-0261), May 5, 2020
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: Rationalization process: an engineering asset needs forecast first, then a review of asset needs, safety, reliability, growth, resource constraints, rate impacts, customer input and financing that cut the forecast by about $50M a year; top four drivers (customer service requests, failure risk, system capital investment support, capacity constraints); Cambrian MTS needed because South Nepean reached the limits of local transformation capacity, leave to construct applied for May 2019, approved October 2019, energization Q2 2022; System Renewal and System Service merged for tracking because funds shift between them; commitment to ISO 55000.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa interrogatory responses CCC-46 to CCC-79 (EB-2019-0261), including Attachments CCC-56(A) and CCC-60(A) and (B): METSCO review of Hydro Ottawa's Asset Condition Assessment framework (May and October 2019)
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: ACA input data held in PowerDB (substation tests) and GIS Mobile Inspector (distribution inspections), manually extracted into Excel 'data loaders' that calculate health indices; calculation errors found in the Excel files; health index results loaded into Copperleaf C55 for risk evaluation while investment prioritization was still done in Excel; HI converted to probability of failure and risk cost for station assets; 12 major asset classes reviewed (4 station, 4 overhead, 4 underground); station assets need at least 70% of data, six of eight station classes below 50% sample size; METSCO first engaged January 2019, initial assessment May 2019, follow-up October 2019 for a fixed $17,000; revised maintenance cycles (annual transformer visual and infrared, vault inspections every 3-6 years, annual XLPE cable testing).

sources.title: Filing Requirements for Electricity Distribution Rate Applications, 2021 Edition for 2022 Rate Applications, Chapter 5 Consolidated Distribution System Plan (June 24, 2021)
sources.supports: A DSP sets out asset management and capital expenditure plans over a minimum five-year forecast period plus five historical years; investments justified by reference to the asset management process; section 5.2.2 requires evidence of coordinated planning with the transmitter, IESO and regional planning deliverables; project or program justifications above the materiality threshold; asset condition assessment and prioritization methods described.

sources.title: Ottawa Sub-Region: Integrated Regional Resource Plan (March 4, 2020)
sources.supports: Regional planning runs on a five-year cycle: Needs Assessment led by the transmitter, Scoping Assessment and IRRP led by the IESO, then a Regional Infrastructure Plan; for Ottawa the Needs Assessment was released in June 2018, scoping completed September 2018 and the IRRP published March 2020; LDCs produce 20-year station-level gross demand forecasts from known connection applications and typical customer demand, starting from IESO weather-normalized 'unbundled' gross demand; a net extreme-weather planning forecast is used to test station capacity.

sources.title: Scorecard - Hydro Ottawa Limited (2017-2021) and 2021 Scorecard Management Discussion and Analysis
sources.supports: DSP implementation progress measured as actual over planned System Renewal and System Service spending; 92% in 2021, missed because planned work was deferred for labour availability, material availability and pandemic outage restrictions; emergency spend $8.57M against a $6.73M budget, driven by poles and underground transformers.

sources.title: Hydro Ottawa 2022 OEB Custom Incentive Rate Progress Report
sources.publisher: Hydro Ottawa Limited (OEB Regulatory Document Search)
sources.supports: Capital spending tracked against approved amounts by budget program (about 35 programs across System Access, System Renewal and Service, General Plant); 2021-2022 cumulative gross capital $276.4M actual vs $282.3M approved; System Service 26% under approved (capacity upgrades, SCADA, communications deferred) while System Renewal ran over; May 2022 derecho damaged more than 500 poles, cost $24M including $15.3M capital, the equivalent of four years of emergency replacements in two weeks; fleet replacement delayed by supply chain; wood pole replacement unit cost $8,415 (2021) and $9,951 (2022) against an $8,510 target.
